lines.text: {first} looks you up and down and says nothing at all.
"You again. Say what you want and be quick about it."
"You've a nerve, talking to me after what you said."
"There's my helper! My back still thanks you for yesterday."
"Word is you sorted out that business for us. Ashford owes you a drink."
"Gods, you're bleeding. Get yourself to the herbalist before you fall over."
"You look half-starved, {kid}. The inn does a fair stew."
"{greeting}" {first} waits a beat. "...You're meant to say '{reply}'. Where'd you grow up, a barn?"
"Hm? Oh. Hello, {kid}. Does your mother know where you are?"
"Stranger in the square. Well, not for long in a village this size. I'm {first}."
"Morning, {player}. The dew's still on the barley."
"Afternoon. Hot work, whatever the work is."
"Evening, {player}. Heading for the inn? Everyone is."
"Bit late to be out, isn't it? The stones only keep so much away."
"Past your bedtime, {kid}. Home with you."
"{player}! Good to see a friendly face."
"Ah, it's you. Pull up a barrel, I was just about to stop for a breather."
"If it isn't my favourite {kid} in Ashford. What's the news?"
"{player}. I was hoping you'd come by. Walk with me a moment?"
"Soaked to the bone. Rain's good for the fields and bad for everything else."
"Can't see the end of the lane in this fog. Don't wander off the road."
"Thunder like that, the old ones say the Flame is turning in its sleep."
"Fire answered your Blessing, they say. The smithy could use hands like that."
"Water-blessed, are you? The temple's healers would take you in a heartbeat."
"Wind at your back from the Blessing itself. The scouts always want fast feet."
"Earth-blessed. Steady as stone, that's what they'll say of you."
"Lightning, I heard. Careful with that temper of yours, {kid}."
"A dual Blessing! The whole village is still talking about it. Some sect will come sniffing around, mark my words."
"No Blessing at all, they say. Well, plenty made something of themselves without one."
"Sweet on someone, are you? The whole square's noticed how you look at them."
"Betrothed! Well, it's about time. When's the wedding?"
"Married life suits you. Give my best to your spouse."
"Hello there."

choices.text: "I'm sorry for what I said before."

lines.text: "Can't complain. Well, I can, but who'd listen?"
"Tired. The {role} never rests, not in Ashford."
"The fields are coming on. If the wolves leave the sheep be, it'll be a fair year."
"Prices at the stall would make a saint swear. Salt's dear since the road got dangerous."
"Quiet on the walls. Quiet is good. Quiet is what they pay me for."
"Duskbriar's full of good oak and bad things. I cut near the edge and keep my ears open."
"The smith's got me hauling charcoal again. My arms'll be as thick as his one day."
"Better for seeing you. Truly."
"What's it to you?"

choices.text: "What do you think of the Crown these days?"

lines.text: "Hearth and kin, {kid}. Keep your fire lit, keep your word plain, and never turn a traveller from the door."
"We keep the stones. Every spring we scrub the runes on Stonewake and every winter we relight our fires from the brazier on Kindling Night."
"Rank's earned here, not born. My grandfather was a Guard and he ate at the Captain's table."
"King Aldric's old, and the Princess is sharp. Taxes are fair enough. It's the orcs in the south they ought to worry about."
"The Crown sends a tax man twice a year and a soldier never. That's the Crown for you."
"Say what you like about Kingsreach, the King's Ember Road's safe by day. Mostly."
"Not much to tell. Sheep, rain, taxes. The usual."
"We spoke about village gossip before, didn't we? Here's what people are saying now: {rumour}"
"We've already had a turn at gossip, haven't we? Nothing else worth passing on just now."
"{rumour}"
{first} lowers their voice. "{hint}"
{first} leans in close. "I shouldn't say, but you're a friend. {hint}"
"Gossip? With you? Ha."
"That's all I know. Ask at the inn, they hear everything there."
"{rumour}"
"Not a thing, thank you."
"Help? From you? I'd sooner ask the goat."
"You don't know me, {kid}. Maybe once you do."
"As it happens, there's something. Hear me out."
"The woodpile won't stack itself, if you've an hour to spare."

choices.text: "I'll do some chores for you. (1 hour)"

lines.text: An hour of stacking, sweeping and hauling later, {first} claps you on the shoulder. "You're a good sort."
"Look at that. Done in half the time. Here, have an apple for your trouble."
{first} stiffens. "I'll remember that."
"Charming. Your mother would be proud."
"...Hm. Well. Words are cheap, but it's a start."
